title: Isolated types: one formula determines a complete description

based_on.title: Model Theory Lecture Notes
based_on.pages: 84 (§7.2, isolation and Lemma 7.6); 90 (§7.3, Theorem 7.17, finite type equivalences); notes dated 2018-12-14

summary: Determine when one formula specifies a complete type, and prove that finitely many types are equivalent to all types being isolated.
abstract: In an infinite set with equality alone, two elements either coincide or differ. Each alternative determines every first-order fact about the pair, even though there are infinitely many formulas to consider. A type is called isolated when one formula determines its entire description in this way. For a complete theory with a model, an isolated type has a realization in every model, so any type omitted somewhere must be nonisolated. We prove that there are only finitely many types of a fixed tuple length exactly when every type of that length is isolated. Equality patterns and ordered groups of equal coordinates then give explicit finite classifications for infinite sets and dense orders without endpoints.
